items.t: The page covers the unincorporated community of Lake Errock, on the lake of the same name near Harrison Mills, east of Mission. Every first-page card in the research was labelled with the board sub-area "Lake Errock" and a "Mission" mailing address, on streets including Bayview Road, Malcolm Road, Morris Valley Road and Lougheed Highway. Note the feed's own spread: first-page cards run from Bayview Road on the lake to Morris Valley Road and a Lougheed Highway manufactured-home park address that also appears in the Dewdney-Deroche feed — the board line and the community line are not the same thing.

Planning frame: the governing plan is the FVRD's Electoral Area C Official Community Plan, Bylaw 1747, 2024, adopted by the Regional Board on September 18, 2025, which includes a dedicated Lake Errock Neighbourhood Plan; it replaces the former consolidated OCP Bylaw No. 0020, 1998 (titled for "Portions of Area C: Morris Valley, Harrison Mills, Lake Errock"). Lake Errock's designations, development permit areas and zoning under Bylaw 1747 and the Neighbourhood Plan, for a specific lot: UNVERIFIED in the research pass — the new bylaw's Lake Errock schedules have not been read.

Neighbours, as references only: Harrison Mills (west, in the same Electoral Area C plan area), the District of Kent / Agassiz (east, across the Harrison River side), and Mission (west, the nearest city) — none of them governs Lake Errock.
The FVRD's own election notice places "Harrison Mills–Lake Errock portion of Area C" voters in the School District No. 75 (Mission) rural trustee election, alongside Deroche (Area G) voters.

The lake itself: the live feed's own cards describe Lake Errock as a boat-restricted lake used for kayaking and paddleboarding, with a channel connection toward Harrison Lake — that is listing-card text, not an official source; the lake's boating restrictions, public access points and any FVRD regional-park status on an official page: UNVERIFIED.

Servicing and hazards: feed listing text references Fraser Health-approved perc tests, geotechnical hazard assessments and drilled wells on building lots — servicing here is lot-by-lot (well/septic) on the face of the listings, but no FVRD servicing page for Lake Errock was opened in the research pass, so community water/sewer availability for any specific lot is UNVERIFIED. The former Area C OCP (Bylaw No. 0020, 1998) included geological-hazard and environmentally-sensitive development permit areas; whether Bylaw 1747 carries the same areas for Lake Errock, and parcel-level status for any lot: UNVERIFIED.

Transit, commute and health care: no TransLink or BC Transit service summary for Lake Errock was opened in the research pass, no official source states commute times in minutes, and the nearest hospital on an official Fraser Health page is UNVERIFIED in that pass. Listing-card drive-time claims ("20 mins to Mission") are not adopted.

items.t: Planning and zoning (local): the FVRD's Electoral Area C Official Community Plan, Bylaw 1747, 2024 (adopted September 18, 2025), covers Lake Errock and includes a Lake Errock Neighbourhood Plan — it replaced the former OCP Bylaw No. 0020, 1998 — and FVRD zoning applies lot by lot. City of Mission and District of Kent plans do NOT apply.

Manufactured-home pad rent (MHPTA): for any pad-rent manufactured home in the feed, the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act rent-increase limit is 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026, and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027 — confirmed from the park's own tenancy documents for any specific pad.

blocks.text: Good to know about Lake Errock

items.t: The plan for this community is brand new. The FVRD adopted a new Electoral Area C Official Community Plan — Bylaw 1747, 2024, adopted September 18, 2025, with a dedicated Lake Errock Neighbourhood Plan — replacing a consolidated plan from 1998 (Bylaw No. 0020).

The mailing address is the trap, again. Every card says "Mission," the page title says "Mission BC Waterfront," and Lake Errock is in no municipality at all — zoning, permits, servicing and taxes run through the FVRD (Electoral Area C) and the Province.

There is no school to walk to, in either direction, without a district check. No school sits in Lake Errock on the Ministry record; the FVRD notice ties the area to SD75 trustee elections, SD78 schools sit across the river at Agassiz, and no catchment document for a Lake Errock address was opened — a family buying here is buying a drive, in a district they must confirm first.

"Waterfront" here is a claim, not a tenure. The lake's boating restrictions, public access points and park status were not confirmed on any official page in the research pass, and no dock or moorage right for any listed property was confirmed — the water is the reason people buy here, and it is the least verified part of the package.

items.t: Governance: Lake Errock is unincorporated land in FVRD Electoral Area C. The FVRD's Area C Official Community Plan page states the plan area "spans from the Harrison River to the east of Deroche and includes Morris Valley, Harrison Mills, Lake Errock, and the eastern portions of the Deroche Bench." The current plan is the FVRD's Electoral Area C Official Community Plan, Bylaw 1747, 2024, adopted by the Regional Board on September 18, 2025, which includes a dedicated Lake Errock Neighbourhood Plan; it replaces the former consolidated OCP Bylaw No. 0020, 1998.

Note the feed's own spread: first-page cards run from Bayview Road on the lake to Morris Valley Road and a Lougheed Highway manufactured-home park address that also appears in the Dewdney-Deroche feed — the board line and the community line are not the same thing.

Where the townhouse stock concentrates: nowhere. There is no townhouse corridor, townhouse subdivision or townhouse complex in the community on any source checked. The stock is waterfront and view houses on Bayview Road, large rural parcels and building lots on Malcolm Road and Morris Valley Road, estate-style homes in the Morris Valley corridor developments, and manufactured homes including a Lougheed Highway park address shared with the Dewdney-Deroche feed.

Transit and commute: no TransLink or BC Transit service summary for Lake Errock was opened in the research pass, and no official source states commute times in minutes: UNVERIFIED. Listing-card drive-time claims ("20 mins to Mission") are not adopted.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Lake Errock

items.t: Why this section still matters with zero townhouse stock: a Lake Errock buyer comparing a Morris Valley strata lot (Tapadera, Eagle Point, River Reach) against a city townhouse elsewhere needs both halves — the strata rules that DO apply to those bare-land and single-family stratas, and the fee-simple reality that governs most of the community. Both are stated below, kept separate.

Form B diligence (any strata purchase here — Tapadera LMS648, Eagle Point, River Reach): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. For a bare-land strata the Form B is also where lot-use rules (RV / park model / manufactured home permissions) are proved — listing text is not proof.

Local plan — FVRD, not a city: the governing plan is the FVRD Electoral Area C Official Community Plan, Bylaw 1747, 2024 (adopted September 18, 2025), including the Lake Errock Neighbourhood Plan; it replaces OCP Bylaw No. 0020, 1998. Tapadera's own development guide refers to a Consolidated Zoning Bylaw No. 1638, 2021 for Holiday Park requirements — a guide's reference, not the bylaw text, carried here as UNVERIFIED for zoning purposes. A specific lot's designation, permit areas and permitted dwellings: UNVERIFIED — confirm with the FVRD for the PID.

SSMU / suites in FVRD ground: Feed cards claiming "R-2 zoning allowing a coach house" (Malcolm Road building lots) are listing text only and are not adopted. Do not apply Surrey's, Mission's or any city's SSMUH tiers here.

ALR frame (applies parcel by parcel): any Lake Errock-area parcel in the Agricultural Land Reserve follows the ALC housing frame — one principal residence at a maximum of 500 m², a secondary suite only inside the principal residence, plus at most one additional residence of 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha). ALR stratification bar: ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)) — a farm property cannot be converted into townhouse strata lots. Whether a specific parcel is in the ALR: UNVERIFIED at parcel level — one feed card claims a lot is "Out of the ALR" in listing text, which is not verification.

BC Assessment farm thresholds (full three-tier form, where farm class is claimed): $2,500 of farm income for parcels of 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the value of land over 4 ha for larger parcels; $10,000 for parcels under 0.8 ha; applications by October 31.

RURAL property tax regime — explicitly different from Mission's: Lake Errock is unincorporated, so the owner receives the property tax notice from the Province's Surveyor of Taxes Office and pays property taxes to the Province, not to the FVRD or any city. Under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act s. 11, rural property taxes are due July 2, a 5% penalty is added to any portion unpaid on July 2, and a further 5% penalty is added to any portion unpaid on October 31. Do NOT apply the City of Mission's flat 10% penalty or any city's staged dates here.

items.t: The Electoral Area C OCP, Bylaw 1747, 2024, was adopted September 18, 2025 and includes a dedicated Lake Errock Neighbourhood Plan, replacing Bylaw No. 0020, 1998 — any marketing quoting the old plan's designations for a lake lot is quoting a replaced document, and any specific lot's new designation is UNVERIFIED until the FVRD confirms it for the PID.

Two different "strata" products share one road and neither is a townhouse. Morris Valley Road carries a bare-land RV/park-model strata (Tapadera, LMS648, Harrison Mills side) and detached estate-home stratas (Eagle Point, River Reach) within a short drive of each other — a buyer comparing monthly fees across them is comparing a recreation lot's services against a golf-course estate's, not two versions of the same purchase.

The lake's boating character is listing text, not an official finding. Feed cards describe Lake Errock as a boat-restricted lake used for kayaking and paddleboarding with a channel connection toward Harrison Lake — the lake's boating restrictions, public access points and any regional-park status on an official page are UNVERIFIED in this research. Confirm frontage, dock tenure and boating rules on title and with the FVRD/Province before marketing water access.
The feed mixes a Dewdney-Deroche park address into the lake page. A search saved on this page alone will surface product that is not in the lake community.

There is no Lake Errock price figure to quote. SnapStats publishes no median, $/sq ft, sale-to-list or days-on-market figure for the sub-area — pricing evidence has to come from the property's own comparables, and Mission's published medians describe a city market across the river.

items.t: Fee-simple lots are the default form: the feed's lake houses, cottages and acreages — including a 13-acre Bayview Road property and 3.71- and 3.73-acre Malcolm Road building lots, each described in listing text as R-2 zoning allowing a coach house — are fee-simple parcels unless title says otherwise: no strata corporation, no Form B, no strata fees. The "R-2" labels and lot details are listing-card text only, not verified zoning. A community-wide strata-versus-freehold split is UNVERIFIED — no official source publishes one.

Bare-land strata — its own form, documented here as land: Tapadera Estates, 14600 Morris Valley Road — BARE-LAND STRATA (Strata Plan LMS648): A bare-land strata lot IS strata tenure on the lot itself — Form B, strata fees for common property and registered bylaws apply to the lot; it is NOT fee-simple, and a lot with an RV, park model or manufactured home on it is still bare-land strata. Its listings also describe it as a Harrison Mills community, so its presence in the Lake Errock feed is board-line spillover — follow the address, not the feed label. Unit/lot count: UNCONFIRMED as a published figure.

: Fresh-verified in the townhomes pass (Nov 2, 2026): a current listing records Sub-Type Single Family Residence, built 2017, Title to Land Freehold Strata, on the 11th fairway at Sandpiper Golf Course. Detached estate homes on strata lots are single-family strata — the lot carries strata tenure even though the house form is detached. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED.

Serviced vs unserviced ground, as the sources state it: feed listing text references Fraser Health-approved perc tests, geotechnical hazard assessments and drilled wells on building lots — servicing here is lot-by-lot (well/septic) on the face of the listings, but no FVRD servicing page for Lake Errock was opened in the research pass, so community water/sewer availability for any specific lot is UNVERIFIED. Obtain the actual reports and confirm they are current and transferable before valuing a build.

Hazard and riparian diligence sorts the building lots: geotechnical and riparian assessments recur in the feed's building-lot cards, and the former Area C OCP (Bylaw No. 0020, 1998) included geological-hazard and environmentally-sensitive development permit areas for its plan portions — whether Bylaw 1747 carries the same areas for Lake Errock, and parcel-level hazard or permit-area status for any lot, is UNVERIFIED.

The lake itself: the feed's cards describe Lake Errock as a boat-restricted lake used for kayaking and paddleboarding, with a channel connection toward Harrison Lake — that is listing-card text, not an official source; the lake's boating restrictions, public access points and any FVRD regional-park status on an official page are UNVERIFIED. "Waterfront," dock and boat-access language in listing text is not a right — confirm frontage and dock tenure on title and with the FVRD/Province.
ALR vs non-ALR split: no split is published and none is stated. One feed card claims a lot is "Out of the ALR" in listing text, which is not verification.

Assemblies / development sites / rezoning proposals, documented AS SUCH, never as inventory: none is documented in this area's research. Matsqui-style assembly language does not apply here; no proposal is named or counted.
: No phase selling vacant lots is documented for Lake Errock. Never mixed with built presales.

faq.q: Is Lake Errock part of Mission?
faq.a: No — for mailing and board reporting it carries a Mission address and the board groups its name under Mission, but Lake Errock is an unincorporated Fraser Valley Regional District Electoral Area C community: the FVRD's Area C Official Community Plan page names Lake Errock among the communities in its plan area, and the City of Mission does not govern it.

faq.q: Is there a market statistic for Lake Errock?
faq.a: For counts, yes: SnapStats carries a Lake Errock sub-area row under the Mission board grouping — September 2026 recorded 16 detached listings with 1 sold (6% sales ratio) and 1 Condos & Townhomes listing with 0 sold (ratio NA). But no median or other price figure for Lake Errock is published — SnapStats publishes medians at community level only, and Mission's community medians are not Lake Errock's (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: What governs building on a Lake Errock lot?
faq.a: The Fraser Valley Regional District: its Electoral Area C Official Community Plan, Bylaw 1747, 2024 (adopted September 18, 2025), covers Lake Errock and includes a Lake Errock Neighbourhood Plan — it replaced the former OCP Bylaw No. 0020, 1998 — and FVRD zoning applies lot by lot; a specific lot's designation, permit areas and permitted dwellings must be confirmed with the FVRD for the PID.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Lake Errock?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board figures showed 16 houses listed with 1 sold in the month and 1 condos and townhomes listed with 0 sold in the month in Lake Errock. Those are month-end counts and move daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Lake Errock a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In September 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 6%, a buyers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: Are there any condos in Lake Errock?
faq.a: None verified — no condo building in this community was confirmed on an official, developer or strata source in the research, and no townhome complex was confirmed either. The verified stock is lake houses, cottages, acreages, estate-style homes and manufactured homes.

faq.q: Who do I pay property tax to on a Lake Errock property?
faq.a: The Province: rural-area properties receive their tax notice from the Surveyor of Taxes Office and pay the Province, not the regional district or a municipality; rural taxes are due July 2, with a 5% penalty on amounts unpaid on July 2 and a further 5% on amounts unpaid on October 31 (Taxation (Rural Area) Act, s. 11).

faq.q: Where do Lake Errock children go to school?
faq.a: 75 (Mission), whose nearest confirmed schools are Dewdney Elementary and Deroche Elementary — but the catchment assignment, and even the district boundary (SD75 vs SD78) for a specific Lake Errock address, is UNVERIFIED.

faq.q: Can I actually buy a townhouse in Lake Errock?
faq.a: A buyer who needs a townhouse is looking at Mission, Chilliwack or Harrison-area city stock, not the lake.

faq.q: Tapadera Estates looks like a townhouse park — what am I buying?
faq.a: A bare-land strata lot (Strata Plan LMS648) that you own, for an RV, park model or manufactured home under the strata's lot-development rules — with a strata fee, a Form B package and strata bylaws, not a pad rental and not a townhouse. Fresh listings call it "Freehold bareland strata" in terms.

faq.q: Eagle Point charges a monthly fee — is it a townhouse strata?
faq.a: No — it is Freehold Strata in single-family form: detached estate homes on strata lots beside Sandpiper Golf Course (a current listing records Sub-Type Single Family Residence, Title to Land Freehold Strata). The fee buys strata services (grounds, management, snow removal on the listing record), and the diligence is still the Form B — but the built form is a house, not a townhouse.

faq.q: Who do I pay property tax to, and what is the penalty?
faq.a: The Province (Surveyor of Taxes), under the rural regime: due July 2, 5% on amounts unpaid July 2 and a further 5% on amounts unpaid October 31 (Taxation (Rural Area) Act s. 11). Mission's flat 10% city penalty does not apply here.

faq.q: What is a bare-land strata lot at Tapadera Estates?
faq.a: Strata tenure on the lot itself (Strata Plan LMS648) — you own the lot as a strata lot, pay strata fees for the common property (clubhouse, pool, river access on the strata's own site), and take a Form B; an RV, park model or manufactured home on the lot does not change the tenure. It is not fee-simple.
